why: The inbox tool sorts by alias, so the alias a public page publishes decides where a real reader's email lands. Before 2026-08-18 every public page published ops@ - the internal catch-all the sorter routes AROUND - so reader mail arrived unsorted. This map makes the alias a property of the page's PURPOSE, and scripts/validate-public-email-aliases.mjs fails the build when a page publishes an alias that does not match its purpose (or publishes ops@ at all).
never_public_reason: ops@ is the internal default the inbox tool sorts around. A public page publishing it defeats the sorter for every message it attracts.

aliases.support: Contact, support, corrections, and general user-facing help
aliases.privacy: Privacy policy, consumer health data, and data-subject requests
aliases.hello: General and about pages with no more specific purpose
